title: Other Chicago-era musicians: Maxson, Bargy, Stitzel, Danny Alvin
summary: They run through Roy Maxson, the Benson Orchestra, Defoe, Mel Stitzel and Danny Alvin, with Ashcraft knowing few well.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh, there were a couple of people around Chicago, and I'm trying to think. Uh, they, they, uh, got in, uh, the trombonist Maxson. Remember him?
Yes. What was his name? Uh, Roy. Roy. Roy Maxson. Sure. Yeah. Wasn't he with White Man later?
Uh, yes.
Yeah.
And, uh, he's from New Orleans.
No, I didn't know that. Yeah.
And, uh...
I think I knew him. And the Benson Orchestra, if you remember, had, uh, Roy Bargy in it. And, uh, a couple saxophone players that ended up with White Man.
Of course you got to know Valle Defoe.
I, I never knew him well at all. I'd met him.
Well, he was a slightly earlier generation, I think. He was about, uh...
I saw him a few years ago.
And, um... There were a few who, uh...
Mal Stitzel.
Yes.
Is another. Who played the piano with the Rhythm Kings.
Well, I thought surely I could remember four or five of them. Uh, where does Danny Elvin... Is he, uh... Was he a little older?
Uh, he must have been, because I don't remember him as of then at all.
Got into show work.

I think, as a matter of fact, I probably first met him in New York. And then back here later. Uh, we were talking about, uh, Tony Perennis from New Orleans. Yes. Isn't he? Yes. I can't remember how early I knew him anymore.
